source_text: [1] Καὶ ὑμῖν δὲ πρέπει μὴ συγχρᾶσθαι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου, ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν θεοῦ πατρὸς πᾶσαν ἐντροπὴν αὐτῷ ἀπονέμειν, καθὼς ἔγνων καὶ τοὺς ἁγίους πρεσβυτέρους οὐ προσειληφότας τὴν φαινομένην νεωτερικὴν τάξιν, ἀλλ’ ὡς φρονίμους ἐν θεῷ συγχωροῦντας αὐτῷ, οὐκ αὐτῷ δέ, ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τῷ πάντων ἐπισκόπῳ. [2] εἰς τιμὴν οὖν ἐκείνου τοῦ θελήσαντος ἡμᾶς πρέπον ἐστὶν ἐπακούειν κατὰ μηδεμίαν ὑπόκρισιν: ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὅτι τὸν ἐπίσκοπον τοῦτον τὸν βλεπόμενον πλανᾷ τις, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀόρατον παραλογίζεται. τὸ δὲ τοιοῦτον οὐ πρὸς σάρκα ὁ λόγος, ἀλλὰ πρὸς θεὸν τὸν τὰ κρύφια εἰδότα.
pass_a_gloss: And it is fitting for you too not to take advantage of the bishop's youth, but to give him all respect according to the power of God the Father, just as I know that the holy presbyters too have not taken advantage of his apparently youthful rank, but, as men wise in God, they yield to him; yet not to him, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the bishop of all. So, for the honor of him who desired us, it is fitting to obey without any hypocrisy, since it is not that a person deceives this bishop who is seen, but he cheats the one who is unseen. In such a case the reckoning is not with flesh but with God, who knows the hidden things.

lemmas.gloss: make use of, take advantage of

pass_b_english: You too must not presume on your bishop's youth. According to the power of God the Father, render him every mark of respect. I know that the holy presbyters also have not presumed on his rank, young as it appears. As men wise in God they defer to him; not to him, though, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the Bishop of all.

To honor the One who has desired us, then, it is fitting to obey without any pretense. For a man does not deceive this bishop who is seen; he cheats the Bishop who is unseen. In such a case the reckoning is not with flesh but with God, who knows what is hidden.

choices.why: The verb means to treat something as usable for oneself; the fault is exploiting, not merely noticing, his age.
Title of the Father; capitalized as a divine title, and it sets up the seen/unseen bishop contrast.
rejected: the overseer of all (loses the wordplay)

choices.why: A reckoning word (false accounting), matched by 'his account' below for ὁ λόγος.

choices.english: the One who has desired us
choices.why: θέλω with a personal object: God has willed or wanted us.
rejected: him who has willed us [so to do] (supplement)

anf_compare.notes: Minor. ANF renders οὐ προσειληφότας τὴν φαινομένην νεωτερικὴν τάξιν as 'not judging rashly from the manifest youthful appearance'; the Greek says the presbyters did not take advantage of his apparently youthful rank. ANF 'seeks to mock' is loose for παραλογίζεται (cheat by false reckoning). Rest same sense.

notes: 'God, who knows the hidden things' may echo Romans 2:16 or Psalm 44:21; not cited inline because the wording is general.

review.notes: p1 checked in full. 'Καὶ ὑμῖν δὲ πρέπει μὴ συγχρᾶσθαι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου' matches A 'it is fitting for you too not to take advantage of the bishop's youth' and B 'You too must not presume on your bishop's youth'; 'ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν θεοῦ πατρὸς πᾶσαν ἐντροπὴν αὐτῷ ἀπονέμειν' is kept as respect according to the Father's power. 'καθὼς ἔγνων καὶ τοὺς ἁγίους πρεσβυτέρους οὐ προσειληφότας τὴν φαινομένην νεωτερικὴν τάξιν' and 'οὐκ αὐτῷ δέ, ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τῷ πάντων ἐπισκόπῳ' are preserved (A 'yet not to him, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the bishop of all'; B 'not to him, though, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the Bishop of all'). 'ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὅτι τὸν ἐπίσκοπον τοῦτον τὸν βλεπόμενον πλανᾷ τις, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀόρατον παραλογίζεται' keeps the seen/unseen contrast and the τις-agent (A 'it is not that a person deceives this bishop who is seen, but he cheats the one who is unseen'). 'τὸ δὲ τοιοῦτον οὐ πρὸς σάρκα ὁ λόγος, ἀλλὰ πρὸς θεὸν τὸν τὰ κρύφια εἰδότα' matches both reckoning clauses. No inline citation is present to mismatch; the note withholds a verse because the wording is general. Title names the young/unseen contrast, not only the locus.

Paragraph 1: Locked Greek contains two sentences. Pass A renders 'καὶ ὑμῖν δὲ πρέπει μὴ συγχρᾶσθαι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου' as 'And it is fitting for you too not to take advantage of the bishop's youth', which matches the sense. Pass B renders it as 'You too must not presume on your bishop's youth', which is synonymous and adds no contradiction. The clause 'κατὰ δύναμιν θεοῦ πατρὸς πᾶσαν ἐντροπὴν αὐτῷ ἀπονέμειν' is translated in Pass A as 'to give him all respect according to the power of God the Father' and in Pass B as 'According to the power of God the Father, render him every mark of respect' — both preserve agency (God the Father as source of power) and modality (obligation). The relative clause 'καθὼς ἔγνων καὶ τοὺς ἁγίους πρεσβυτέρους οὐ προσειληφότας τὴν φαινομένην νεωτερικὴν τάξιν, ἀλλ’ ὡς φρονίμους ἐν θεῷ συγχωροῦντας αὐτῷ, οὐκ αὐτῷ δέ, ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τῷ πάντων ἐπισκόπῳ' is rendered in Pass A as 'just as I know that the holy presbyters too have not taken advantage of his apparently youthful rank, but, as men wise in God, they yield to him; yet not to him, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the bishop of all' and in Pass B as 'I know that the holy presbyters also have not presumed on his rank, young as it appears. As men wise in God they defer to him; not to him, though, but to the Father of Jesus Christ, the Bishop of all' — both preserve the negation (οὐ προσειληφότας), the agency (presbyters yielding), the contrast (not to him but to the Father), and the title (τῷ πάντων ἐπισκόπῳ as 'bishop of all' / 'Bishop of all'). The second sentence begins 'εἰς τιμὴν οὖν ἐκείνου τοῦ θελήσαντος ἡμᾶς πρέπον ἐστὶν ἐπακούειν κατὰ μηδεμίαν ὑπόκρισιν' — Pass A: 'So, for the honor of him who desired us, it is fitting to obey without any hypocrisy', Pass B: 'To honor the One who has desired us, then, it is fitting to obey without any pretense' — both preserve the purpose (honor), the agent (the One who desired us), the obligation (πρέπον ἐστὶν), and the negation (μηδεμίαν ὑπόκρισιν → 'without any hypocrisy/pretense'). The clause 'ἐπεὶ οὐχ ὅτι τὸν ἐπίσκοπον τοῦτον τὸν βλεπόμενον πλανᾷ τις, ἀλλὰ τὸν ἀόρατον παραλογίζεται' is rendered in Pass A as 'since it is not that a person deceives this bishop who is seen, but he cheats the one who is unseen' and in Pass B as 'For a man does not deceive this bishop who is seen; he cheats the Bishop who is unseen' — both preserve the negation (οὐχ ὅτι ... πλανᾷ τις), the agency (a person deceives / cheats), the contrast (seen vs. unseen bishop), and the verb choice (παραλογίζεται → 'cheats' per lemmas). The final clause 'τὸ δὲ τοιοῦτον οὐ πρὸς σάρκα ὁ λόγος, ἀλλὰ πρὸς θεὸν τὸν τὰ κρύφια εἰδότα' is rendered in Pass A as 'In such a case the reckoning is not with flesh but with God, who knows the hidden things' and in Pass B as 'In such a case the reckoning is not with flesh but with God, who knows what is hidden' — both preserve the negation (οὐ πρὸς σάρκα), the contrast (not with flesh but with God), and the agency (God as knower of hidden things).
